result.title: VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters
result.summary: Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. We propose VIBRA, which matches relevance on the old gallery, corrects the errors of a single model with the barycenter of several views, which is itself a query in the old space, and trains the new encoder to inherit this consensus, so that models absent at deployment still shape every query. We show that the barycenter gains margin over the average of its views exactly when their hardest irrelevant items differ, and we characterize the share of this gain that one encoder can reach. On five benchmarks with five upgrades among six CLIP, MetaCLIP and SigLIP2 backbones, VIBRA is the best compatible method in all 50 settings, improving Recall@1 by up to 5.6 points over the strongest baseline and by up to 18.0 points over the old model, while adding less than 1 ms to the latency of the new encoder.

AI.brief_summary: VIBRA 研究跨模态检索的后向兼容升级：不重编码旧库，而是用多个视图的重心（本身是旧空间中的查询）纠正单模型误差，并把这一共识蒸馏给新编码器，在五个基准的 50 个设置上取得最佳兼容效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先聚合成共识重心、再蒸馏进单一编码器」的做法，可能为 LVR 中多种 latent 假设的聚合、贡献分配与监督提供可核查线索；但论文面向检索编码器兼容性，与推理状态生成无直接关系，迁移性需自行判断。
